meta.disclaimer: 仅供参考，非法律建议 (For reference only, not legal advice). Fees are set by each council and usually reviewed every April; figures reflect the official source as found on 2026-11-16 and may have changed. Always confirm the current fee, licence conditions and planning position on the council's official website before applying. Control-area proposals noted as pending are not law until formally designated.
meta.method: All fee figures were taken from official council pages, fee schedules or policy PDFs found via free web search (browser.search and Parallel free-tier web_search / web_fetch) and, for two documents, browser.open. Figures that could only be found on third-party sites were NOT used; the affected fee_range is null with an explanation in notes. Control-area status was checked against gov.scot (only Edinburgh and Badenoch & Strathspey designated) plus each council's own pages; proposed/pending designations are noted as not in force.

control_areas_in_force: City of Edinburgh (whole council area, since 5 September 2022)
Highland Council — Badenoch and Strathspey ward (since 4 March 2024)
national_framework.control_areas_note: gov.scot (Short-term lets: regulation information, updated 15 May 2026) names only these two designated control areas. In a control area, mandatory condition 13 (planning) may apply: a change of use to a short-term let that requires planning permission must have permission applied for or granted before a licence application. Outside control areas, planning permission may still be required case-by-case if the let is a material change of use.
national_framework.fine: Operating a short-term let without a licence is a criminal offence: maximum fine £2,500, plus a possible ban from applying for a licence for one year.
national_framework.licence: Mandatory short-term let licensing across Scotland since 1 October 2022 (Civic Government (Scotland) Act 1982 (Licensing of Short-term Lets) Order 2022). New hosts must obtain a licence from their local council before taking bookings or receiving guests. A licence usually lasts 3 years.
